speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: First, we need to be clear on what are the primary causes of the drug problem which lead to children being affected.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The Member's question focuses on measures to engage the children of drug-abusing parents, to prevent them from becoming drug offenders themselves.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Looking at this narrowly, from that perspective, will not give an accurate picture.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The primary issue is the trafficking and pushing of drugs in society.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: If we do not deal with those issues upstream, before the harm is caused, then there will be serious consequences to the lives of people and loss of children.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: So, we have to focus on deterring and disrupting the supply of drugs.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: If we do not do that properly, the children will suffer neglect at best from their families and many will face the risk of getting into a life of crime and drugs.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Downstream efforts to help the children, will really be like fighting against the tide in such situations.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: We are very concerned about the children and the other people affected by drugs.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: That is why we take a tough approach on drugs.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: I will ask the Member if he agrees with the tough approach we have taken on drugs, the approach to severely punish the traffickers and suppliers responsible for this problem, if we are concerned about children, then I assume the Member will agree with us.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Every year I can name you a case of such a child.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Five years old, four years old, parents affected by drugs.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The court heard that his mother, who had thrown the hot water on him, told the IMH psychiatrist that she had abused meth for years and that she was probably suffering from withdrawal symptoms in the days before the boy's death, because she was unable to buy drugs from her usual supplier.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: In such cases I asked Members, what could have been done to save the child, which is part of the question the Member is asking.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: What we have done is to save the lives of thousands of such children with our focus on preventing widespread use of drugs through our very tough drug policies; probably one of the only country, if not, one of the few countries in the world that have dealt with this problem effectively.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: That helps prevent such cases from happening in the first place.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: We could identify the problem accurately if we want to find the right solutions.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: I have tried to explain how we try and make sure we reduce, minimise the risks of the situation that the Member has been referring to, from even arising in the first place.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: But despite all our efforts, and despite our tough laws and stance, there will be persons who will continue to abuse drugs and place their families and children at risk.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: In those cases, how do we help the children?

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The Government works closely with the community to help them.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Newly admitted offenders are encouraged to participate in the Yellow Ribbon Community Project (YRCP).

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Under the YRCP, volunteers reach out to the families of inmates through home visits and link them up with various social support and community programmes.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: This is real hard work on the ground.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Not glamourous, but thousands of people going, spending thousands of hours, helping.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Prisons will also refer inmates and their family members who require assistance to the Family Resource Centres, (FRCs).

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: FRCs operate from the Prison Link Centre in Changi.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: They render financial assistance, accommodation and social assistance.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Where necessary FRCs will refer the families to the Family Service Centres (FSCs) for further casework support within the community.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: FSC social workers will try and review the family's risks and needs, and coordinate intervention and support across different agencies.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: For school-going children, FSCs will also link up with the schools to discuss their needs – the types and level of support needed by the children.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Besides FSCs, we also have youth agencies, which provide support services for children and young persons who have behaviours which put them at risk, or who require constructive engagement.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: These include mentoring programmes, interest-based activities and career coaching.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Then, there is the aspect of parent-child bonding.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: It provides inmates with family-centred programmes, like the Social Skills Training Programme and the Family Reintegration Programme, to equip them with communication skills, to engage their children and loved ones more effectively.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: In the past five years, Prisons has provided about 21,000 programme places to inmates for this purpose.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Prisons also works with various other community partners on programmes and services, aimed at addressing the impact of the parents being in jail.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: These include counselling, tuition assistance, parenting programmes and family bonding programmes, for example, run by The Salvation Army, Centre For Fathering and the Singapore Children's Society.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Over the last two years, 282 inmates and their families attended these programmes.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The Member has also asked about how do we evaluate the effectiveness of these programmes?

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: I think the first question is, when I lay this out, I think Members will agree that this has to be done.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: I cannot believe that any Member here would say, we should not do any of these or should be cutting back on these.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: In terms of quantifying it, this is a very difficult to study, because there are too many factors that are outside of Prisons' control.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: So, it is not an area you can easily quantify.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: You have to make an assessment and go ahead and do it; as we have been able to convince thousands of volunteers to do, together with Prison's officers and NGOs which see the benefit of doing these activities.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Prisons generally look at how the effectiveness of its various programs can be assessed.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: So, you are talking about 20 years or so.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: A good way to start the morning, Minister.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: It was really about acknowledging that this is a serious issue, the drug problem, especially internationally.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: And certainly, I would support a tough stance against drugs.
